newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Hart says has 19.9 pct of Burns Philp.
newsitem.headline: Hart says has 19.9 pct of Burns Philp.

text.p: New Zealand investor Graeme Hart said in a substantial security holder notice that he had increased his relevant interest in yeast and spices group Burns Philp & Co Ltd to 19.9 percent from 16.24 percent.

Hart made the statement in a notice filed with the New Zealand Stock Exchange on Friday, confirming comments he made earlier in the week to a newspaper that he wanted to move to 19.9 percent ownership.

Hart's Australian brokers, Deutche Morgan Grenfell, bought over 3.5 percent of Burns Philp stock at A$2.50 a share on Wednesday and is believed to have put it aside for Hart while he gains government approval to go beyond the 14.9 percent threshold for foreign investors.

Hart would have to launch a full takeover bid for Burns Philp under Australian corporate law if he wanted to go beyond 19.9 percent, or wait for six months to use the law's 'creep' provisions to increase his stake by three percent every six months after that.

Brokers said A$2.50 was a top price to pay for Burns Philp, which is planning to sell its herbs and spice businesses to focus on its yeast business, while at the same time it is involved in ongoing litigation over the Estate Mortgage Trusts.
Estate Mortgage, for which a Burns Philp subsidiary was trustee, collapsed in 1990 with A$600 million in losses.
Burns' shares were unchanged at A$2.45 at 2.55 p.m. (0455 GMT).
